parts.text:
The amount of time, in minutes, spent by a customer on one visit to a certain shop is modelled by the random variable $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. In the past, the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$ were 10.5 and 3.8 respectively. The shop has recently moved to a new location, and the manager hopes that the new value of $\mu$ will be greater than 10.5. He takes a random sample of 10 customers and notes the time they each spend in the shop. He then calculates the sample mean $\bar{x}$ for these 10 times.

Using a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level, the manager finds that there is sufficient evidence to conclude that the new value of $\mu$ is greater than 10.5.

Stating a necessary assumption, find the smallest possible value of $\bar{x}$.
